ca_harlequin_dome.blurb: Harlequin Dome is a steep, south-facing dome of granodiorite rising above Tenaya Lake in the Tuolumne area of Yosemite. Ten routes are listed, nearly all traditional, with a single bolted line. Grades run from 5.10 to 5.12, centred on 5.11, so it suits climbers who are already comfortable leading hard cracks and faces. Most lines take one to three pitches, though several wander rather than follow a straight crack. Because the wall takes the sun all day, it feels warm, and the walk in is short and easier than at neighbouring domes.
ca_harlequin_dome.parking_note: Use the lot at the Tenaya Lake picnic area on the east end of the lake, then walk across Highway 120 to the foot of the dome.
ca_harlequin_dome.approach: From the lot, cross the highway and scramble up low-angle slabs to a short headwall. The far left side of it goes with two or three easy 5.0 moves. Above, a well-worn trail leads to the base of the cliff.

ca_mouth_the.blurb: The Mouth is the best-known formation within Lizard's Mouth, a sandstone bouldering area in the Santa Ynez Mountains near Santa Barbara. It mixes six boulder problems with four top-rope lines. The boulder problems start at easy V0 and top out at a single V6, though most are V3 or easier. The roped lines span the 5.10 to 5.13 range and are climbed on a top rope, with a large overhang adding interest. A popular traverse across the face makes a good warm-up. Only a few minutes from the car, it attracts many visitors, so weekdays and early mornings are quieter.

ca_dragon_s_lair_the.blurb: The Dragon's Lair is a bouldering pocket within Potter's Point, in the mountains above Santa Barbara, centred on a sizeable cave formed by two huge boulders leaning together, with a tree growing between them. Ten sandstone problems climb the blocks, and the grades stretch from V3 through the V4 to V5 range up to V11, so it is mostly a venue for strong boulderers. Many of the lines are committing. Potter's Point generally has very coarse, abrasive rock that is hard on skin, and some of it is loose, so test holds and bring pads and a spotter.

ca_horseshoe_canyon.blurb: Horseshoe Canyon is a side canyon in the Cave Valley climbing area of the Auburn State Recreation Area in the Sierra foothills. It has ten bolted sport routes and is known for some of the harder climbing in the Auburn area, with four lines in the 5.12 range and four at 5.10, plus one easy and one moderate route. The routes mostly face north and stay shaded through the day. The right-hand wall is more than 200 feet tall, but most lines currently top out at about 75 feet. New routes are still being added occasionally.
